questions.explanation: Goniometer vs inclinometer example. (Reliability)

questions.q: A test with high SENSITIVITY is best used to:
options: Rule OUT a condition when negative
Rule IN a condition when positive
questions.explanation: Specificity: positive rules in. (Reliability)

questions.q: In the Functional Reach test example in Parkinson's (9 TP, 21 FN, 12 TN, 1 FP), sensitivity was:
questions.explanation: 9/(9+21) = 30%; specificity 12/13 = 92%. (Reliability)

questions.q: The MDD formula is:
questions.explanation: Example 6MWT: MDD90 ≈ 61 m, MDD95 ≈ 73 m. (Reliability)

questions.q: Using Cohen's criteria, an effect size of 0.6 is:
questions.explanation: ≤0.2 small, 0.2–0.5 moderate, >0.5 large. (Reliability)

questions.q: In normal standing, which muscle is constantly active?
questions.explanation: Soleus and erector spinae also active; gluteus maximus and abdominals quiescent. (Posture)

questions.q: What proportion of body weight is over the heels in normal standing?
questions.explanation: Forefoot 30–47%, midfoot 1–8%. (Posture)

questions.q: In the lateral postural view, the plumb line should:
options: Bisect the acromion and pass slightly anterior to the lateral malleolus
questions.explanation: Posture lecture.

questions.q: Lower crossed syndrome features tight:
options: Thoracolumbar extensors, iliopsoas and rectus femoris
questions.explanation: Weak deep abdominals and gluteus maximus/medius. (Posture; Lumbar)

questions.q: Upper crossed syndrome features WEAK:
options: Deep cervical flexors, middle/lower trapezius (and rhomboids)
questions.explanation: Posture; Cervical (Janda 1988).

questions.q: Which test assesses static motor balance?
questions.explanation: Posture lecture.

questions.q: The Romberg coefficient in posturography compares:
options: Sway area with eyes open vs eyes closed
questions.explanation: OE SSKG / CE SSKG. (Posture)

questions.q: In spectral analysis of sway, the high-frequency zone (2–20 Hz) reflects:
questions.explanation: Zone 1 0–0.5 Hz, zone 2 0.5–2 Hz. (Posture)

questions.q: The screw-home mechanism refers to:
options: Obligatory lateral tibial rotation in the last 5–10° of knee extension
questions.explanation: Due to larger medial condyle; very stable position. (Knee)

questions.q: The knee's loose-packed position is:
options: Full extension with tibial lateral rotation
questions.explanation: Close-packed: full extension + lateral tibial rotation. (Knee)

questions.q: The knee capsular pattern is:
questions.explanation: Knee lecture.

questions.q: Which meniscus statement is from the course?
options: The lateral (O-shaped) meniscus takes about 70% of lateral compartment load
The lateral meniscus takes 10% of load
questions.explanation: Medial is C-shaped and takes about 50% of medial compartment load. (Knee)

questions.q: The normal Q angle is:
questions.explanation: A larger Q angle creates a larger lateral vector on the patella. (Knee)

questions.q: Patellofemoral joint reaction force during a squat is about:
questions.explanation: Walking 1.3 BW, stairs 3.3 BW, squat 7.8 BW. (Knee)

questions.q: The Shelbourne criterion for starting sport-specific training after ACL reconstruction is an extensor deficit below:
questions.explanation: <25% for agility drills, <15% for sport-specific training. (Knee)

questions.q: Which H:Q ratio is the only one affected in the ACL-deficient knee (Dvir)?
questions.explanation: Aagaard's functional H:Q ratio. (Knee)

questions.q: The normal adult femoral angle of inclination is:
questions.explanation: 150° infants, 125° adults, 120° elderly; coxa valga >135°, coxa vara <120°. (Hip)

questions.q: Excessive femoral anteversion (>12°) is typically compensated by:
questions.explanation: Normal 8–12°. Retroversion → toe-out. (Hip)

questions.q: The hip close-packed position is:
options: 20° extension with slight internal rotation and abduction
questions.explanation: Loose-packed 30° flex/30° abd/slight ER. (Hip)

questions.q: The hip capsular pattern is:
options: Equal limitation of flexion, abduction and internal rotation, little/no loss in ER
questions.explanation: Hip lecture.

questions.q: During single-leg weight bearing, the hip abductors must produce a force of about:
questions.explanation: Hip lecture.

questions.q: Weak hip abductors are associated with:
options: Medial lower-extremity collapse (dynamic valgus) and patellofemoral pain
questions.explanation: Also correlated with low back pain. (Hip)

questions.q: The acetabulum is formed mainly by:
questions.explanation: Hip lecture.

questions.q: Low back pain lifetime prevalence quoted in the lumbar lecture is:
questions.explanation: Lumbar lecture.

questions.q: Which ligament is about 80% elastin and resists flexion?
questions.explanation: ALL resists over-extension. (Lumbar)

questions.q: The lumbar capsular pattern is:
options: Marked equal restriction of side bending, then flexion and extension
questions.explanation: Lumbar lecture.

questions.q: Sacral nutation means:
options: The sacral base moves anteriorly while the inferior part moves posteriorly
questions.explanation: Counternutation is the reverse, resisted by the long dorsal ligament. (Lumbar)

questions.q: The posterior oblique subsystem consists of:
options: Contralateral gluteus maximus and latissimus dorsi with the thoracolumbar fascia
Ipsilateral biceps femoris and erector spinae
questions.explanation: Deep longitudinal subsystem: erector spinae, TLF, sacrotuberous ligament, biceps femoris. (Lumbar)

questions.q: The flexion–relaxation phenomenon is:
options: Reduced lumbar erector spinae activity in maximal trunk flexion
questions.explanation: Often delayed or absent in LBP. (Lumbar)

questions.q: In professional golfers, which side-bridge R/L difference cut-off predicted LBP?
questions.explanation: Sensitivity 100%, specificity 63%. (Lumbar)

questions.q: The atlanto-axial joint is responsible for approximately:
questions.explanation: Cervical lecture.

questions.q: In the lower cervical spine, side bending and rotation occur:
questions.explanation: Cervical lecture.

questions.q: The general cervical capsular pattern is:
options: Side bending and rotation equally limited; extension more limited than flexion
questions.explanation: Cervical lecture.

questions.q: The SCM produces:
options: Ipsilateral side bending and contralateral rotation
questions.explanation: Cervical lecture.

questions.q: Normal deep neck flexor endurance values quoted are about:
options: 39 s in men and 29 s in women
questions.explanation: Domenech et al. 2011. (Cervical)

questions.q: Which spinal nerve relation is specific to the cervical spine?
options: Each nerve exits above its vertebra (C8 below C7)
Each nerve exits below its vertebra
Nerves exit through the vertebral body
questions.explanation: In the lumbar spine nerves exit below the corresponding vertebra. (Cervical; Lumbar)

questions.q: Isokinetic dynamometry is considered:
options: The gold-standard dynamic strength test, with good reliability
questions.explanation: Evaluation systems lecture.

questions.q: An isokinetic peak-torque deficit is considered relevant when it is:
questions.explanation: Deficit = (1 − PT involved / PT uninvolved) × 100. (Evaluation systems)

questions.q: Isokinetic reliability is generally HIGHER at which joints?
questions.explanation: Caruso et al. 2012. (Evaluation systems)

questions.q: The manual muscle test is described as:
options: Of low reliability, non-linear and not useful in upper motor neuron disease
questions.explanation: Hand-held dynamometers are reliable. (Evaluation systems)

questions.q: A limitation of 2D video gait analysis is:
options: It gives no information about kinetics and can hide movements
questions.explanation: Evaluation systems.

questions.q: Inverse dynamics combines kinematic data with force-plate data to calculate:
questions.explanation: Positive power = concentric; negative = eccentric/absorption. (Evaluation systems)

classes.title: Research Methodology
classes.desc: Scientific method, PICO, hypotheses, objectives, Research Protocol rules

questions.q: How is Research Methodology assessed?
options: 40% individual MCQ final exam, 60% group Research Protocol
questions.explanation: Theoretical part 40% (MCQ exam), practical part 60% (Research Protocol). (Evaluation document)

questions.q: The Research Protocol's 60% is divided into:
options: Preliminary evaluation 20%, final submission 20%, final presentation 20%
questions.explanation: Group formation is not weighted. (Evaluation; Lesson 1)

questions.q: According to Lesson 1, the passing requirement is:
options: Passing both the RP and the exam (each mark ≥ 5)
questions.explanation: The evaluation document also states that a total score of 5 is required; otherwise BCE. (Lesson 1; Evaluation)

questions.q: How big are Research Protocol groups?
questions.explanation: 14 groups of 5–6; choose a coordinator. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: Who evaluates the Research Protocol?
questions.explanation: Àlex Chicano runs the final exam. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: During an RP review appointment:
options: No changes to the score will be made – the aim is to improve skills
The score can be raised on request
The whole group must attend and argue the grade
questions.explanation: Only one member requests the review by e-mail. (Evaluation)

questions.q: A research protocol is:
options: The written plan of the study, setting out its structure
questions.explanation: Also used for grant funding and IRB approval; scientifically it organises research logically and efficiently. (Lesson 1, anatomy of research)

questions.q: The "physiology of research" refers to:
options: How research works – drawing inferences from findings
questions.explanation: Anatomy = what it is made of (study plan); physiology = how it works. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: Internal validity is:
options: The degree to which the investigator draws correct conclusions about what actually happened in the study
How well results generalise to people outside the study
The reliability of a measurement tool
questions.explanation: Inference #1. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: External validity (generalisability) is:
options: The degree to which conclusions apply to people and events outside the study
The accuracy of conclusions inside the study
questions.explanation: Inference #2. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: "Empirical" means:
questions.explanation: Empirical evidence can only come from research. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: Which order of the scientific method was presented?
options: Observe → research → hypothesis → test → analyse/conclude → share results
questions.explanation: Example: movement sonification for walking after stroke. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: Which databases were named for the research step?
questions.explanation: Lesson 1, scientific method step 2.

questions.q: A research question is:
options: The uncertainty the investigator wants to resolve by performing the study
questions.explanation: Lesson 1.

questions.q: Which is a required property of a good research question?
options: It must be testable and lead to a falsifiable hypothesis
It must already have a known answer
It must be impossible to measure
questions.explanation: It should have a real answer, be testable, lead to a falsifiable hypothesis, and be ethical and relevant. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: A "falsifiable" hypothesis means:
options: There must be a possible negative answer to it
It is based on false data
questions.explanation: Lesson 1.

questions.q: In Lesson 1's description of an experiment, the control group is:
options: What the experimental group is compared against
The group receiving the new treatment
questions.explanation: An experiment includes an experimental group and a control group. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: If experimental results concur with the hypothesis's deduced consequences:
options: The hypothesis is verified; otherwise it is falsified
The hypothesis is automatically proven forever
questions.explanation: Lesson 1.

questions.q: For a new investigator without an experience base, a recommended source of research questions is:
questions.explanation: Others: careful observation of patients, staying open to new ideas and technologies. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: What does PICO stand for?
questions.explanation: A format to help define the research question. (Lesson 1; RP Guidelines)

questions.q: In "virtual reality vs conventional rehabilitation for upper-limb function in chronic stroke", the Comparison (C) is:
questions.explanation: P = chronic stroke patients, I = VR, O = upper-limb functionality. (Lesson 1 example)

questions.q: What does SMART stand for in objectives?
questions.explanation: Lesson 1.

questions.q: Objectives in the research protocol should start with:
options: A verb in the infinitive (e.g. to assess, evaluate, determine)
A verb in the past tense
questions.explanation: Structure: verb – intervention – outcome – population; one objective per outcome. (Lesson 1)

questions.q: How many objectives should each study outcome have associated with it?
options: Each outcome should have an associated objective
Only the primary outcome needs one
questions.explanation: Lesson 1.

questions.q: The stroke epidemiology slide stated that stroke affects about:
options: 15 million people worldwide every year, with ~30% first-year mortality
questions.explanation: Severe disability in two-thirds of survivors (Pu et al., 2023). (Lesson 1)

questions.q: The RP assignment consists of:
options: A brief introduction and an extensive methods section of a research protocol
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: The knowledge-gap (relevance) section may be at most:
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: The hypothesis section must include:
options: A null and an alternative hypothesis
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: In the study design section you must explain:
options: The study arms and which guidelines you will follow to describe procedures
questions.explanation: Plus a flow chart. (RP Guidelines)

questions.q: The randomisation section must state:
options: The method used and who will perform it
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: The blinding section must describe:
options: The procedure used and who will be blinded
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: Which element describes the MATERIALS used in the intervention?
questions.explanation: Brief name, what, who provided, how, where, when and how much. (RP Guidelines)

questions.q: The "HOW" element of the intervention describes:
options: Mode of delivery (face-to-face or tele-rehabilitation) and individual vs group
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: The "WHEN AND HOW MUCH" element includes:
options: Number of sessions, schedule, duration, intensity and dose
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: The expected change in the main outcome for the sample size should take into account the:
questions.explanation: If MCID is not established, use previous similar studies; source suggested: Rehabilitation Measures Database (sralab.org). (RP Guidelines)

questions.q: When choosing statistical tests in the data analysis section you must consider:
options: The type of variable, the number of groups and the number of assessment time points
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: The ethics section must reference:
options: The Declaration of Helsinki and the Ethics Committee, with a mandatory Informed Consent form
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: References in the RP must follow:
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: The RP must be written in which verb tense?
questions.explanation: It is a protocol for a study not yet performed. (RP Guidelines)

questions.q: Which font and spacing are required?
options: Arial, Calibri or Times New Roman 10–11, line spacing 1.5
questions.explanation: Titles may use a different size; text in black. (RP Guidelines)

questions.q: Which pages must be numbered?
options: Every page except the title page
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: What happens if information is placed in the wrong section?
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: Late uploads of the RP to Moodle are:
questions.explanation: RP Guidelines.

questions.q: The RP front page and index must be:
questions.explanation: Front page: university, students, teacher, course, date; plus a summary page. (RP Guidelines)

questions.explanation: Syllabus marking criteria. (The intro slides once say 40% for the midterm; the syllabus is authoritative.)

questions.q: The midterm exam consists of:
questions.explanation: No minimum mark is required for the midterm. (Syllabus; presentation)

questions.q: When is the midterm exam?
questions.explanation: Calendar.

questions.q: The final exam differs from the midterm because it:
options: Has negative marking and requires a minimum of 4.5/10

questions.q: What happens if a student misses their oral presentation?
options: They are referred directly to the BCE
They present alone the next week
questions.explanation: All group members must present; grades are individual. (Syllabus)

options: Topics related to the classes and how they influence decision-making and physiotherapy treatment
A literature review on pharmacology history only

questions.explanation: Calendar.

questions.topic: Core definitions (from Nóra's study pack, not lecture slides)
questions.q: The WHO defines health as:
options: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease
questions.explanation: Study pack, week 1 (WHO definition).

questions.topic: Core definitions (from Nóra's study pack, not lecture slides)
questions.q: "Illness" refers to:
options: The person's subjective, lived experience of disease
questions.explanation: Disease = disrupted structure/function with identifiable aetiology/pathogenesis. (Study pack)

questions.topic: Core definitions (from Nóra's study pack, not lecture slides)
questions.q: Aetiology is:
options: The sequence of events from cause to lesion
questions.explanation: Pathogenesis = sequence of cellular/tissue events from cause to lesion; morphology = structural changes. (Study pack)

questions.topic: Core definitions (from Nóra's study pack, not lecture slides)
questions.q: Which is a SIGN rather than a symptom?
questions.explanation: Signs are objective; symptoms are subjective. (Study pack)

questions.topic: Core definitions (from Nóra's study pack, not lecture slides)
questions.q: Which is often called the "fifth vital sign"?
questions.explanation: HR, RR, BP, temperature, SpO2 and pain. (Study pack)

questions.topic: Core definitions (from Nóra's study pack, not lecture slides)
questions.q: The biopsychosocial (ICF) frame matters to physiotherapists because:
options: The same pathology does not mean the same disability
questions.explanation: ICF components: body functions/structures, activities, participation, environmental and personal factors. (Study pack)
